identity.title: Evidence for the Disruption of a Planetary System During the Formation of the Helix Nebula

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we combine infrared (SOFIA, *Spitzer*, *Herschel*) and millimetre (ALMA) observations of the system to determine the origin of this excess using multi-wavelength imaging and radiative transfer modelling.

question.value: What is the origin of the infrared excess around the Helix Nebula central white dwarf WD 2226-210: remnant planetesimal belt, cometary cloud, or post-AGB disc?

evidence.quote: The origin of this excess is ambiguous. It could be a remnant planetesimal belt, a cloud of comets, or the remnants of material shed during the post-asymptotic giant branch phase.

claims.hypothesis: The excess is a remnant post-AGB circumbinary disc
claims.experiment: CO/SiO limits plus SED grain-size constraint
claims.result: No gas detected; grains too small compared to the 60 µm blow-out size

evidence.quote: We therefore discard the idea of a post-AGB circumbinary disc as the potential origin for the excess emission.

claims.hypothesis: The excess is a compact remnant planetesimal belt
claims.experiment: SED and radiative transfer models compared to ALMA upper limit
claims.result: Steep SED needs small grains well below blow-out size

evidence.quote: The non-detection of millimetre wavelength emission from the system therefore counts against the planetesimal belt hypothesis for the origin of the observed excess.

claims.hypothesis: The dust is delivered by a cometary cloud
claims.result: About 5,000 Hale-Bopp equivalent comets per year
claims.finding: Disrupted planetary system is the preferred origin

evidence.quote: This leads us to conclude that the excess emission observed around the central white dwarf in the Helix Nebula originates from the disruption of a massive Kuiper belt analogue.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Post-AGB disc and in-situ planetesimal belt destruction rejected

evidence.quote: The observed dust emission is inconsistent with either a remnant of the post-AGB envelope or the in-situ collisional destruction, or sublimation, of remnant planetesimals
